intro: Distillation transfers a teacher’s distribution over alternatives. Temperature smooths both distributions and changes the scale of their gradients.
task: Compute T-squared-scaled mean KL(teacher||student) and the gradient with respect to student logits.
requirements: student and teacher are matching batch-by-classes logit matrices, with at least two classes. temperature T is a scalar in [0.1,100].
Apply stable log-softmax to logits/T. Return {"loss": T*T*mean(sum(q*(log(q)-log(p)), axis=1)), "gradient": T*(p-q)/batch}, with q=teacher probabilities and p=student probabilities.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Subtract the row maximum before exponentiating and calculate log probabilities without logging underflowed probabilities.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Differentiating logits/T cancels one factor of the T-squared loss scale.

explanation: KL direction matters: the teacher distribution weights the comparison. A student matching the teacher exactly has zero loss and zero gradient at every supported temperature.
The T-squared multiplier is a training convention that compensates for much of the gradient shrinking caused by smoothing. The teacher logits are fixed targets in this exercise.
